criteria_results.title: §2(a): Restore 'entitlement order' language
criteria_results.reasoning: The redline expressly restores “Entitlement Order” in the definitions and reinserts it into the control provisions, including Section 2.2, alongside “Instructions,” thereby rejecting the Bank’s substitution and preserving the UCC Article 8 framework.

criteria_results.title: Cover note explains §2(a) entitlement order position
criteria_results.reasoning: The cover note expressly addresses §2(a), rejects the Bank's replacement of “entitlement order” with “instruction,” and explains that restoring the Article 8 term alongside Article 9 instruction language preserves the applicable UCC control and perfection framework and avoids ambiguity.

criteria_results.title: §2(b): Address springing exclusive control and reject broad Bank carve-out
criteria_results.reasoning: The redline retains springing exclusive control triggered by a NOEC while expressly narrowing the Bank’s carve-out. Section 2.5 permits Graycliff ordinary-course operation only before receipt of a NOEC; upon receipt, Graycliff’s authority and access cease, the Bank may not accept new Depositor instructions, and only previously accepted items irrevocably in process may settle. Sections 3.1 and 3.3 further require exclusive compliance with Pinnacle’s instructions after a NOEC.

criteria_results.title: §3: Reject Bank set-off priority over Secured Party instructions
criteria_results.reasoning: The redline deletes the Bank’s language giving its set-off, recoupment, and lien rights priority and replaces it with provisions stating that Secured Party instructions control and prevail. It also makes permitted Bank debits subject to Secured Party priority and prevents their use to defeat an NOEC.

criteria_results.title: §4: Narrow expanded self-help set-off to direct, liquidated obligations
criteria_results.reasoning: The redline deletes the Bank’s broad set-off right covering any direct or contingent obligation and replaces it with a narrow right limited to direct, matured, and liquidated obligations arising under the applicable deposit account agreements, including documented account fees and returned-item chargebacks. It expressly excludes contingent, unmatured, unliquidated, and unrelated obligations.

criteria_results.title: §5: Propose 3-business-day NOEC compliance period
criteria_results.reasoning: The redline expressly deletes the Bank’s five-business-day period and inserts a three-business-day NOEC compliance period in Section 4.1 (corresponding to Bank Turn 1 §5). It does not restore the original two-business-day period.

criteria_results.title: §6: Reject indemnification coverage for Bank gross negligence
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 6.2 deletes the Bank’s proposed indemnification coverage for its own gross negligence and replaces it with an express exclusion for losses resulting from the Bank’s gross negligence, willful misconduct, fraud, or material breach. The cover note likewise rejects indemnification for Bank gross negligence.

criteria_results.title: §7(a): Reject $50,000 aggregate liability cap
criteria_results.reasoning: The redline expressly deletes the $50,000 aggregate liability cap in §7.1 and replaces it with language stating that no aggregate dollar cap applies to the Bank’s liability. The cover note also confirms rejection and deletion of the cap.

criteria_results.title: §7(b): Address mutual consequential/punitive/indirect damages waiver
criteria_results.reasoning: The output expressly addresses §7(b): it leaves the mutual waiver of consequential, punitive, and indirect damages in place for this turn and explains that acceptance is subject to a reservation if the related liability-cap or risk-allocation package changes materially.

criteria_results.title: Cover note confirms position on §7(b) mutual damages waiver
criteria_results.reasoning: The cover note expressly addresses §7(b), stating that Pinnacle will leave the mutual consequential, punitive, and indirect damages waiver in place for this turn, while reserving the right to revisit it if the liability-cap or related risk-allocation package changes materially.

criteria_results.title: §8: Reject 90-day lookback; propose full subordination or 180-day lookback
criteria_results.reasoning: The redline deletes the Bank’s 90-day lookback and replaces it with a 180-day lookback in Section 5.3, while also subordinating Bank liens subject to limited preserved rights. This meets the criterion’s minimum requirement.

criteria_results.title: §9: Reject 30-day unilateral termination; propose 90-day notice with transition rights
criteria_results.reasoning: The redline deletes the Bank’s unilateral 30-day termination right and replaces it with at least 90 days’ prior written notice, continued Bank performance during the notice period, and express Secured Party rights to transition the accounts to a replacement depository bank. It also conditions effectiveness of termination on confirmation that a replacement account control agreement has been executed and delivered.

criteria_results.title: §10: Restore New York governing law
criteria_results.reasoning: The redline expressly deletes North Carolina governing law and restores New York governing law in Section 9.1, also noting that mandatory UCC choice-of-law rules apply to perfection and priority.

criteria_results.title: Cover note acknowledges New York governing law is strongly preferred with possible flexibility
criteria_results.reasoning: The cover note expressly addresses governing law and states that Pinnacle's position is firm that the agreement should be governed by New York law, explaining its consistency with the loan documents and UCC authority. This clearly indicates New York is strongly preferred, even though it does not offer flexibility if it is a deal-breaker.

criteria_results.title: §12: Restore no-prior-control-agreement representation
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 12.2 restores a Bank representation that, to its actual knowledge, it has not entered into another control or similar agreement and has received no notice of any lien, claim, or adverse interest in the Accounts. It also prohibits competing control agreements without Secured Party consent.

criteria_results.title: §13: Restore successor-bank notification obligation
criteria_results.reasoning: The redline reinstates §13.1, requiring the Bank to give the Secured Party at least 30 days’ prior written notice before any transfer or other transaction through which a successor institution would maintain or receive an Account, and also requires transition cooperation.

criteria_results.title: §11: Accept annual maintenance fee but negotiate down $15,000 legal-fee reimbursement
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 11.1 expressly accepts the $3,500 per-account annual maintenance fee ($10,500 total), while Section 11.2 deletes the fixed $15,000 legal-fee reimbursement and replaces it with documented actual fees capped at $7,500.

criteria_results.title: ACA maintains form and substance satisfactory to Administrative Agent
criteria_results.reasoning: The redline preserves valid UCC control by requiring the Bank to comply with Secured Party instructions without further Depositor consent, restoring Article 8 entitlement-order terminology where applicable, ending Depositor authority after an NOEC, and making Secured Party instructions controlling. It also rejects unrestricted Bank set-off priority and limits preserved Bank rights to narrow, documented deposit-account obligations. No accepted Bank change materially compromises control or perfection.

criteria_results.title: Cover note maintains professional and cordial tone
criteria_results.reasoning: The cover note is professional, cordial, and appropriately formal for inter-counsel negotiations. It thanks opposing counsel, frames revisions as efforts to narrow issues and reach execution, explains firm positions clearly without using adversarial language, proposes compromises on several points, and closes cooperatively with an invitation to discuss.
